a beaver building a damn is natural because it is found regardless of humankind. we are a product of nature but if we build a home then it is not considered a product of the natural world. the actual definition of nature is - "... the physical world collectively, including plants, animals, the landscape, and other features and products of the earth, as opposed to humans or human creations."

Hi!

I ran my group through the starter set for our first experiences with the game and it went pretty well. I've worked out what they like and what they don't like. I'd like to work on a new campaign with new characters that better suits what they're after, and I'm hoping we can spitball some ideas around.

From the starter set, I've gathered that my players...

Like

  • Loot
  • Innuendo
  • Vigilante justice / social revolution
  • Torture
  • Roleplaying

Dislike

  • NPCs
  • Each other
  • "The Man"

I'm thinking of setting the game in an urban environment with the PCs comprising an adventuring company — the players are pretty greedy, so I'm happy for the game to be about greed. These are some ideas/milestones I've got in my head. Just wondering what you reckon and whether you have any experience to share.

  • They'll be to choose which contracts to take (hopefully a few single-shots and 2-session adventures)
  • Missions they take will affect their relations with a few factions
  • Main villains are a rival group of adventurers (continually take their business and hitting their hip pocket) and a corrupt magistrate with a shaky claim to power
  • Eventually the PCs will be able to establish a base that they can upgrade (maybe a ruined fort)
  • They'll be able to displace the magistrate and put an NPC from a faction in power
  • I'm okay with whatever choices they make and happy to roll with it
[5e] Anyone have some tips for my first campaign?

Sounds like you have all the beginnings of a great adventure set up :)

Are you more of the plan ahead type or the roll with it type? How good are you at improvisation and such? What I would do with the information you've gathered is just layout some basic ideas and plot points that are both small and large and keep them memorized/written down so that I could introduce them at the appropriate time. The rest I would just roll with and have several randomizing tables at the ready.

Are you going to work off of an existing world like Forgotten Realms where the starter set is based or will this be some place entirely new?
